cases.title: A detectable fault stays detectable when a second, simultaneous fault is present
cases.input: S04 alone vs S04 + S07 (flatline) at 60 s
cases.expected: S04 is still detected in the combination
cases.actual: {"S04 alone": [["MS_AIRFLOW", 66.2]], "S07 flatline alone": [["MS_SIGNAL", 68.0]], "S04 + S07 flatline together": [["MS_SIGNAL", 68.0], ["MS_AIRFLOW", 66.2]], "S04 + S07 dropout (5 s at 120 s) together": [["MS_SIGNAL", 120.0], ["MS_AIRFLOW", 96.2]], "S07 dropout alone": [["MS_SIGNAL", 120.0]]}
cases.notes: Rules require a valid reference (MAP); S07 flatline on INTAKE_PRESSURE invalidates it, so the S04 pattern is not reported and nothing explains why.

cases.title: A second fault of the same kind starting right after the first event's T+30 boundary gets its own event
cases.input: S07 dropout at 90 s then again at 120.0/120.2/121/125 s
cases.expected: each of the two faults produces its own MS_SIGNAL event
cases.actual: {"S07 dropout at 90 s and again at 120.0 s": 2, "S07 dropout at 90 s and again at 120.2 s": 2, "S07 dropout at 90 s and again at 121.0 s": 2, "S07 dropout at 90 s and again at 125.0 s": 2}
cases.notes: The recorder keeps the first trigger of a kind while an event of that kind is active (window inclusive of T+30), so a new same-kind trigger inside it is dropped; this affects back-to-back 30 s cycles.

cases.title: Every missed injection in the app's RANDOM_FAULTS run has an identified cause
cases.actual: S01@30s/5s: 5 s thermal fault too short for the rule (needs sustained rise); S04@60s/18s: masked by the simultaneous S07 flatline (QA-SIM-038); S07@60s/18s: flatline variant is a known undetected pattern; S07@120s/5s: swallowed: an MS_SIGNAL event from the S07 at 90 s was still active at 120.0 s (QA-EVENT-016); S04@150s/45s: engine already stopped (driving profile ends at ~145 s) - simulator limitation
